mechanism: A VAE compresses raw observations into a compact spatial latent vector z; an MDN-RNN predicts the distribution over future z given z and action, maintaining a hidden state h encoding temporal context. A small linear controller receives only (z, h) as input and outputs actions. Because the world model absorbs perceptual and predictive complexity, the controller's search space collapses — credit assignment is trivial over few parameters. Training the controller inside the model's hallucinated rollouts further decouples policy optimization from expensive environment interaction.
invariant: Separating representation (what the world looks like and how it evolves) from control (what action to take) keeps the controller small regardless of environment complexity. The world model bears the representational burden; the policy is always a lightweight read-off of world-model features.
prediction: A controller trained entirely inside the hallucinated dream world transfers to the real environment and achieves competitive performance; equivalently, a controller operating on raw pixels instead of (z,h) requires far more parameters or training steps to reach the same score.
failure_mode: If the world model's learned distribution diverges from the true environment dynamics — e.g., the agent exploits hallucination artifacts to achieve high dream-world scores via adversarial trajectories — the policy fails catastrophically upon transfer. The mechanism breaks whenever the generative model is systematically miscalibrated in action-relevant regions.
source_excerpt: We can even train our agent entirely inside of its own hallucinated dream generated by its world model, and transfer this policy back into the actual environment... By using features extracted from the world model as inputs to an agent, we can train a very compact and simple policy that can solve the required task.
